long_biography.plain_text:
Four former Arthur Andersen colleagues began sketching a new consulting firm on a restaurant napkin as their employer unravelled. Kevin McCarty helped turn those notes into West Monroe, drawing on technology businesses he had started while studying and an internet practice he built at Andersen.

McCarty made employee ownership part of the firm's operating model and later became its second chief executive. When an outside investor acquired half the business, employees retained the other half and management continued to lead it. As executive chairman, he remains responsible for the board, acquisition strategy and the firm's investment arm.
